installSteps.text: Alternatively, download The Legend of Zelda: Return of the Hylian SE — Solarus directly from the official site at https://www.solarus-games.org/games/the-legend-of-zelda-return-of-the-hylian-se/. Always download from the official source — third-party mirrors of free games are a common malware vector.

Run the downloaded installer and follow the prompts. If Windows SmartScreen warns about an unrecognised publisher, that is normal for open-source projects without a paid code-signing certificate — choose More info, then Run anyway.
Open the downloaded .dmg and drag the app into Applications. On first launch macOS may refuse to open it as unidentified — right-click the app and choose Open to approve it once.
Check your distribution's package manager first, which is usually the easiest route. Otherwise download the AppImage from the official site, mark it executable and run it.

Launch the game and look at the settings menu before your first session — resolution and control defaults are worth checking. The Legend of Zelda: Return of the Hylian SE — Solarus needs roughly small of free disk space.

faq.q: Is The Legend of Zelda: Return of the Hylian SE — Solarus free?
faq.a: The Legend of Zelda: Return of the Hylian SE — Solarus is a commercial title (Free to play), not a free one.

faq.q: How big is the The Legend of Zelda: Return of the Hylian SE — Solarus download?
faq.a: Check the official site for current download size and system requirements.

faq.q: What platforms does The Legend of Zelda: Return of the Hylian SE — Solarus run on?
Do I need an account to play The Legend of Zelda: Return of the Hylian SE — Solarus?
faq.a: There's no account requirement to play — download and go.

set.tagline: Vincent Jouillat's Hyrule adventure returns in a shorter, brisker Solarus remake.
set.description: Return of the Hylian: Solarus Edition remakes Vincent Jouillat's 2006 fan game as a compact single-player action adventure. Explore Hyrule, solve dungeon rooms and fight through Ganon's revived forces with keyboard or a configurable joypad.

systemRequirements.min: A Windows, macOS or Linux build of Solarus compatible with this quest's 1.6.x format, plus space for the 6 MB quest file. Solarus does not publish per-OS CPU, RAM or GPU minimums on the game's page.
systemRequirements.recommended: No separate recommended CPU, RAM, GPU or storage tier is published for this quest. Confirm that the chosen Solarus player can load 1.6.x quests.

min.notes: 6 MB is the quest download only; a compatible Solarus player requires additional storage. No numerical CPU, RAM or GPU requirement is published for this game.

recommended.notes: The developer publishes no distinct recommended hardware tier for this game.

set.launcherInstall.note: The official download is a 6 MB .solarus quest, not a standalone executable. It requires a compatible Solarus player; a tested one-click PlayBound package has not yet been built for Windows, macOS and Linux.

qualityBar.verdict: A small Zelda fan adventure that gets you to the dungeon doors quickly and lets the puzzles do the talking.

set.longDescription:
Return of the Hylian began as Vincent Jouillat's 2006 fan game. Solarus Team later rebuilt it in the Solarus engine, releasing this edition in 2015. It keeps the familiar rhythm of a top-down Hyrule adventure: move between areas, push into dungeons, solve a room, and find the next way forward. The remake is relatively short and approachable. That matters when a fan project asks you to learn a new map of an already familiar world; you can start exploring instead of waiting hours for the first interesting lock and key.

The story follows Link after A Link to the Past. His wish has reunited the Light and Dark Worlds, but it has also brought Ganon and his followers back. That setup gives the quest a clear excuse to revisit old enemies while telling its own small chapter. Solarus's release announcement describes fewer tangled labyrinths and easier puzzles than some of the team's other creations. If you want the densest, most devious fan-made dungeon crawl, this is probably not the one. If you want a complete evening-sized detour through classic Zelda grammar, the pace is the attraction.

The current official download is version 1.2.1, a roughly 6 MB .solarus quest file. It is not a Windows installer or a self-contained executable. You need a Solarus player that can run quests targeting engine version 1.6.x. Solarus offers players a launcher for Windows, macOS and Linux, but compatibility with this older quest should be checked before PlayBound promises an automated install on every platform. The game's own page does not provide numerical CPU, RAM or graphics requirements, so our hardware section records that gap instead of inventing specifications.

A November 2015 Solarus update explicitly added joypad support and customizable commands to Return of the Hylian. That is a real game feature, although the exact layout depends on the pad and player configuration. The quest is a single-player adventure; its controller support does not imply online play, virtual LAN, a party handoff or a dedicated server. The official page credits both Solarus Team and Vincent Jouillat, whose original game supplied the foundation for this remake.

There is a simple reason to keep this one on the radar: it is a complete, free fan game with a modest footprint and a clear sense of pace. Its older engine format is also exactly why we are keeping the PlayBound install claim conservative while we test a packaged player. The adventure is ready to explore; our one-click route still needs that final piece of engineering.
set.whyWePickedIt: A compact, complete Hyrule fan quest can be more inviting than a sprawling one. Solarus Team's remake respects Vincent Jouillat's original while making the route through its dungeons easy to pick up. Verified joypad support broadens who can play it; the older quest format still needs a tested PlayBound package.
set.thatOneThing: Link fixes the split between two worlds and accidentally puts Ganon back on the guest list.

installSteps.text: Download Return of the Hylian: Solarus Edition v1.2.1 from its Solarus game page. The 6 MB .solarus file is quest data, so install a Solarus player compatible with 1.6.x quests before opening it.

Get the Windows Solarus player from the official Solarus downloads page, extract its portable ZIP, and open the quest in the player. Check quest compatibility before treating the current 2.x player as an automatic replacement for 1.6.x.
Get the macOS Solarus player from the official Solarus downloads page and install its DMG. Open the .solarus quest in a compatible player; the quest file itself is not a Mac app.
Get the Linux Solarus player AppImage from the official Solarus downloads page, mark it executable, and open the quest in a compatible player. The .solarus file is not an AppImage.

firstPlaySteps.text: Choose a save slot and configure keyboard or joypad commands in the Solarus game settings before entering the first dungeon.

faq.q: Is Return of the Hylian free?
faq.a: Yes. Solarus distributes the fan quest for free. Its page separately identifies open-source code and proprietary material used under fair use.

faq.q: Does it work with a controller?
faq.a: Yes. Solarus added configurable joypad support to this game in its 2015 1.4.5 update.

faq.q: Does the download run by itself?
faq.a: No. The official 6 MB download is a .solarus quest that needs a compatible Solarus player.

faq.q: Can I play it with friends?
faq.a: It is a single-player adventure. There is no verified online, LAN or dedicated-server mode.
This is the 2015 Solarus remake of Vincent Jouillat's 2006 original, not the original C++ release.

bestFor: Players who want a shorter, approachable Zelda fan quest
People who prefer classic dungeons with configurable joypad controls
notFor: Players looking for multiplayer or a dedicated server
Players who require a verified one-click PlayBound install today
